reference_sql:
SELECT s.city, p.brand, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01'
GROUP BY s.city, p.brand
alternatives: SELECT s.city, p.brand, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units FROM orders o JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-03-01' AND DATE '2025-03-31' GROUP BY s.city, p.brand

WITH march_lines AS (SELECT o.store_id, ol.product_id, ol.quantity FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id WHERE date_trunc('month', o.order_ts) = TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01') SELECT s.city, p.brand, SUM(m.quantity) AS units FROM march_lines m JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = m.store_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = m.product_id GROUP BY s.city, p.brand

other_way.tradeoff: Picking the March lines in a CTE first names that step, but one chain of joins is shorter to read.

solver.query:
SELECT s.city, p.brand, SUM(l.quantity) AS units
FROM order_lines l
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.city, p.brand
